note: Nucleus residency under the resident-service model (architecture 36.5, 36.24; two-tier classification from package 42c). One entry per kernel object linked into the production image (the objects of linker/zephyr80.lk); tools/mapcheck.py fails the build when an object is missing or when a fixed-required object is compiled into the cold areas. Tiers: fixed-required = code that executes, or data that is touched, while the window shows another bank (36.5) - it must link inside 2000h-5FFFh; cold = everything else that belongs to bank 7 (the syscall side, boot, the VFS core, process management and the resident-service loader). There are only these two tiers: every object is placed, and the cold data base follows the linked cold code (no arena, no moves).

tiers.fixed-required: Must be visible in the 2000h-5FFFh fixed core: the gates and transition code, the copy primitives, the IRQ executive, the ROMFS bootstrap reader, the processes' raw entry, common-resident boot/panic code and the stacks. mapcheck rejects a fixed-required object whose bytes link at or above 6000h.
tiers.cold: Belongs to bank 7's cold half (6000h-DFFFh), reached only while the window shows bank 7 (P = 0): the syscall dispatcher and bodies, boot and idle, process management, the VFS core, the resident-service loader and the diagnostics.

objects.reason: common-resident latch and mode gates: the only mapping-changing code, always visible

zero-byte ABS label exporting __kernel_code_end, the exclusive end of the linked cold code; the object emits no linked bytes and carries the derived build/geometry/bank7_end.inc, so it stays out of cold_half (the residency-driven codegen flags cannot propagate down its dependency on the generated include)
namespace root router, FS provider and publication table: reached only through the syscall dispatcher or the service loader, both with P = 0 (production switch-over, package 42b)
the ROMFS FILE provider behind /SYSTEM and its metadata reader, called from the router with P = 0 (package 42b)
bind/call/unbind/ns_enum/chdir/getcwd bodies, reached from the syscall dispatcher with P = 0 (package 42b)
diagnostic syscall bodies, reached only through the syscall dispatcher, which the gate runs with P = 0
extended-memory syscall bodies, the object table and the aperture token (work package 43): reached only through the syscall dispatcher, which the gate runs with P = 0
diagnostic port primitives reached only from the diagnostic syscall bodies (P = 0)
common-resident early console and panic path: must survive any mapping
IRQ registry and dispatch: the executive runs while the window shows the owner's bank (service-owned IRQs), so its code and data stay visible
linked end of the fixed _CODE area and the SDCC IY trampoline used by the IRQ path
common-resident IRQ stubs and gate; it carries the relocated ISR stack (5F00h-6000h) in its own ABS area
CTC quiesce source driver, called by the dispatcher while the owner's window is open
IM2 vector page in common memory: fetched with whatever mapping is active
kernel boot and idle path: every service-facing call returns with the caller's latch restored, so it only ever runs with P = 0
string helpers called by the fixed ROMFS bootstrap reader while the window may show another bank
page-zero RST 30h material: must be present in every mode
common-resident panic path: must survive any mapping
IRQ platform bring-up (IM2 vector page, interrupt mode): common-resident
process lifecycle; the exit notification is a nucleus -> VFS upcall through a fixed shim, so the body is cold
exec/exit and the continuation stack; the executable-stream read is a nucleus -> VFS upcall through a fixed shim
common-resident raw application entry jump: no window-visible state
ROM-resident page-zero reset copier: runs before any mapping exists
common-resident ROM-read stub mirrored into every ROM page (mode 00)
the one ROMFS reader, kept in the nucleus as the bootstrap-reader primitive a bank-6 provider calls through the fixed core
SDCC runtime helpers called from fixed code and from IRQ handlers
common-resident boot entry and C runtime init: runs before the window exists
syscall dispatcher and its bodies: the syscall gate clears the page field before dispatching, so this object only ever runs with P = 0
the syscall transition gate is common-resident by contract (always visible); it saves the caller's whole latch, dispatches with P = 0 and restores exactly
common-resident application-bank copy gate (mode-10 crossings from common memory)

mode-11 window copy for auxiliary slots 3-6 (work package 43): runs with the window showing bank 7 - bank, where only the fixed core and common memory answer; fixed keeps the cost off the scarce common region

revision-13 upcall shim: cold code that calls a resident service saves the latch, selects the window page, calls and restores; its code, its continuation and its request state must stay visible while the window shows another bank (36.5)
VFS core: path walking is production cold code beside the syscall dispatcher and the service loader (the retired stage-5 move left it in bank 7; package 42c placed every object)
VFS core: per-process handles and workspace is production cold code beside the syscall dispatcher and the service loader (the retired stage-5 move left it in bank 7; package 42c placed every object)
The path view a resident service reads: the frame handed to a bank-6 dispatch names the path by address, so the workspace is touched while the window shows bank 6 (36.5's fixed rule)

M10 stage 3 IPC substrate (architecture 36.5, 36.7-36.10): the endpoint table, register/lookup/call, the frame array, the descriptor table and the copy resolvers execute, and are touched, while the window shows bank 6, so they must link inside 2000h-5FFFh.  Linked by the ipc-selftest acceptance image now (test_link); production adopts it in package 41, when the arena drivers leave bank 7.

M10 stage 3 fixed-core IPC primitives (kernel/ipc/ipc_asm.asm): the latch save/select/restore, the window LDIR and the service-stack switch, plus the ABS declaration of the 512-byte service stack at ZOS_SERVICE_STACK_BASE.  Same stage as `ipc`: test images only until package 41.

M10 stage 3 common-resident aperture copy (kernel/ipc/ipc_common.asm, work package 39 correction 01): the path-B primitive runs with mode 10 and page 1 in force, where bank 7 is not mapped, so its code, its request block, its saved latch/SP and its interrupt-push stack must all be common.  The fixed-core reservoir the M9 ledger held back (ZOS_COMMON_M10_RESERVATION) was released to M10 by work package 43 (architecture 36.20), so this primitive and package 43's mode-11 window copy share the whole ceiling.  Same stage as `ipc`: test images only until package 41.

M10 stage 4 resident-service loader (kernel/service/service_loader.c, architecture 36.11/36.12): reads the boot manifest through the fixed ROMFS reader, validates and places every service image through the common application-bank copy gate, and runs the boot segments and hot inits.  It runs with P = 0 only (the syscall gate normalizes before any syscall, and the boot path is mode 11), so the body is cold code; the acceptance image links it now, production adopts it in package 41.

M10 stage 4 service boot gate (kernel/service/service_boot.asm): switches mode 10 over bank 6 (Q = 6) and calls a boot segment.  Its code and continuation execute with bank 7 unmapped, so the gate is common-resident; its request/transition state is fixed-core data because the upcall shim reads the loader's request block with bank 7 mapped.  Same stage as the loader: test images only until package 41.

cold_half_note: The production build compiles these objects into the cold areas (_WINDOW / _WINDOW_DATA at 6000h-DFFFh): the syscall dispatcher and its bodies (including the extended-memory family, package 43), the boot path, the process lifecycle, the VFS core and the resident-service loader (package 42c placed every object; the cold data base follows the linked cold code). tools/mapcheck.py fails the build when the linked cold code or data overruns the derived bases, and the fixed ledger reports the remaining fixed-core bytes.
